title: Potential Energy
seo_title: Grade 8 Potential Energy Worksheets: Gravitational, Elastic and Magnetic Potential Energy
standard_text: Develop a model to describe that when the arrangement of objects interacting at a distance changes, different amounts of potential energy are stored in the system.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on potential energy (NGSS MS-PS3-2): PE = mgh, elastic and magnetic potential energy, how arrangement changes stored energy, and PE changing into KE. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Changing the arrangement changes stored energy.
key_sub: Lifting, stretching, or pulling attracting objects apart stores potential energy in the system: PE = m × g × h.
body_html:
How to think about it

Potential energy is energy stored in a system of objects that push or pull on each other at a distance. Changing their arrangement changes the stored energy.

  • Gravitational PE: lifting an object higher stores more energy. PE = m × g × h (g = 10 N/kg on Earth).
  • Elastic PE: stretching or squeezing a spring or rubber band stores energy.
  • Magnetic and electric PE: pulling attracting objects apart, or pushing repelling objects together, stores energy.

When the objects are released, the PE changes into kinetic energy.

Example

A 2 kg book is on a 1.5 m shelf. PE?

2 × 10 × 1.5

Answer: 30 J

Example

Two attracting magnets are pulled apart. What happens to PE?

Work is done to separate them.

Answer: It increases.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking PE belongs to one object. It is stored in the system.
  • Forgetting g: PE = m × g × h, not m × h.
  • Thinking pulling attracting magnets apart lowers PE.

faq.q: How do you calculate gravitational potential energy?
faq.a: PE = m × g × h. On Earth, g is about 10 N/kg, mass is in kilograms and height is in meters.
In the system of interacting objects, such as a book and Earth, or two magnets, not in one object alone.

faq.q: How does potential energy change into kinetic energy?
faq.a: When objects are released, the stored energy changes into motion. A falling ball loses PE and gains the same amount of KE, ignoring air.

items.q: What unit is used for potential energy?
items.e: All energy is measured in joules.

items.q: What three things does gravitational PE depend on?
c: mass, gravitational field strength and height
items.e: PE = m × g × h.

c: It decreases as it changes to kinetic energy.
items.e: Energy changes form.

items.q: Two magnets attract each other. When do they store the most potential energy?

items.e: Pulling attracting objects apart takes work.

items.e: More stretch, more stored energy.

items.q: A ball sits on the floor. Is the gravitational PE of the ball-Earth system zero?

Only if the floor is chosen as the zero height.
items.e: Heights are measured from a chosen level.
